claim_boundary: U.S. initial unemployment-insurance claims are a high-frequency leading labor-market indicator, but they are volatile, seasonally adjusted and revised. A four-week decline may identify labor resilience that supports risk demand, yet it may also lag or conflict with monetary-policy and inflation channels. Exactly one preregistered long-or-cash audit may test this sign; no causal or alpha claim is imported from the source definition.

feature_contract.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED

prior_matrix.identity: U.S. Employment and Training Administration Initial Claims via FRED
prior_matrix.finding: The official series is a weekly count ending Saturday, seasonally adjusted, sourced from the Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report and tagged Public Domain: Citation Requested.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: The present-vintage series is revised and does not preserve the first advance estimate that was available to a historical decision maker.

prior_matrix.identity: U.S. Department of Labor Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims technical notes
prior_matrix.finding: The weekly release is embargoed until Thursday 8:30 a.m. Eastern; initial claims are described as a leading labor-market indicator, while the administrative data are volatile and difficult to seasonally adjust. Advance claims are revised after subsequent state reporting.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: A leading labor indicator does not imply weekly Bitcoin return predictability, and a present-vintage backtest can benefit from revisions unavailable at the original release.

real_time_design_requirements: Before accessing any historical ICSA values, freeze a source-feasibility specification for exact FRED CSV identity, Saturday weekly lattice, missing-value handling, both-state support, transitions, annual breadth and concentration.

If the source gate permits continuation, seal exact annual FRED CSV responses for ICSA from 2017-01-01 through 2024-12-31; reject duplicate, non-Saturday, non-positive, missing or discontinuous weekly observations.
Compute each current value from exactly four consecutive weekly observations and compare it only with the exact four-week mean ending 28 calendar days earlier.
Make observation week ending Saturday D usable only at D plus seven calendar days 00:00 UTC, after the normally scheduled Thursday release, and valid for at most 168 hours.
Use the same historical BTC corpus, valuation clock, fee, adverse-slippage, cash-yield and capital conventions as the matched buy-and-hold comparator.

Require separate Design and Validation predictive gates before opening matched-capital economics; require return effect, negative-rate effect, drawdown path, annual breadth, support and concentration.

Do not add continued claims, unemployment rate, payrolls, JOLTS, non-seasonally-adjusted claims, recession labels, claims levels, magnitude cutoffs, moving-average alternatives, z-scores, alternate lags, direction inversion, fractional sizing, short legs or post-outcome exceptions.
Do not reinterpret the closed financial-conditions, dollar, yield, liquidity, volatility or credit branches as evidence for this family; labor-market stress is the only proposed mechanism.
Do not open post-2024 data; any historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires separately sealed independent OOS.
uncertainty: Initial claims are volatile administrative data and seasonality can be difficult around holidays, disasters and unusual policy periods.
The present-vintage FRED series contains revisions; the advance values originally available each Thursday and complete revision history remain MISSING_PROOF.
Strong labor data can support risk demand but can also imply tighter monetary policy, so the proposed sign is economically ambiguous.
The four-week comparison and positive risk-demand interpretation are preregistered conventions, not parameters established by the official sources.
No historical ICSA values, BTC outcome, post-2024 observation, candidate, OOS or Trading path was accessed while freezing this prior.
